contract: Every case must produce an identical verdict in the Python contracts and in the JS runtime port. A mismatch means the two implementations have drifted and the JS side is NOT enforcing the plan.

cases.why: a frozen protocol-B apply is a legal manifest
a resolution is a legal manifest
CAS ownership must be storable -- rev18 could not store it, so CAS was a no-op
an unknown CAS status must be rejected, not treated as UNRESOLVED
a frozen resolution would recreate the deadlock it exists to break
every branch is closed (additionalProperties:false)
the autonomous path has no Web capability, so this shape must not validate
the frozen fixture must satisfy single-manifest invariants
a foreign marker would let recovery adopt another operation's commit
CONFLICT must hold authorization for the operator, never spend it
RESOLVED_ROLLED_FORWARD must be a reachable phase
roll-forward must leave authorization consumed
RESOLVED_ROLLED_FORWARD with capability=claimed must be rejected
RESOLVED_ROLLED_FORWARD with receipt=claimed must be rejected -- receipt left claimed is a leak
phase and recorded decision must agree
RESOLVED_ROLLED_BACK must be a reachable phase
rollback must leave authorization available
RESOLVED_ROLLED_BACK with capability=claimed must be rejected
RESOLVED_ROLLED_BACK with receipt=claimed must be rejected -- receipt left claimed is a leak
phase and recorded decision must agree
RESOLVED_ABANDONED must be a reachable phase
abandon must leave authorization available
RESOLVED_ABANDONED with capability=claimed must be rejected
RESOLVED_ABANDONED with receipt=claimed must be rejected -- receipt left claimed is a leak
phase and recorded decision must agree
a correct pair must be accepted
the released capability must be the one the original actually holds
releasing nothing leaks every frozen receipt
releasing a subset leaks the rest forever
naming a receipt the original never held is fabrication
resolvedKind must match the frozen operation
resolvedKind must be a real kind
resolving op A while reporting work on skill B must be impossible
the operator must have seen the current diagnostics
a resolution may not resolve itself
only CONFLICT/PARTIAL hold frozen authorization
the situation must not have moved since review
a capability-less frozen op is resolved with releasedCapId=null
but it may not name a capability that never existed
status=RESOLVED with no decision and phase=CONFLICT permanently freezes the operation: the CAS refuses every new resolution while authorization stays claimed
same permanent freeze via PARTIAL
UNRESOLVED lets a resolution claim it
the same resolution replaying gets its receipt back
a second resolution must be refused (409) -- this is the double-unfreeze guard
already resolved by someone else -> 409
the owner replaying after RESOLVED gets its receipt
an unknown status must fail closed, not default to UNRESOLVED
